pitch: The practical handbook of Intel's former CEO: leverage, indicators, meetings, delegation and one-on-ones.
center: A manager's output is the team's output
quiz: According to Grove's equation, what is a manager's output?
Their own work
The output of their team and of the teams they influence
The number of meetings they run
Their personal revenue
Managers are judged on what the teams they lead or influence produce, not on what they do themselves.
In the breakfast factory, what is the limiting step?
The cheapest step
The longest step, which sets the pace of the whole
The last step
The step given to the intern
Production is organized around the longest step, because it sets the pace.
Why pair indicators?
To double the data
Because focusing on a single indicator causes an unwanted side effect
To impress management
Because it is a legal requirement
Speed and error rate, inventory and shortages: the counter-indicator prevents degrading one aspect while improving another.
Which of these activities has high leverage?
Redoing a competent report's work yourself
Hiring the right person
Attending a meeting with no purpose
Delaying a decision
A good hire has effects for years: it is a very high-leverage activity.
Who owns the one-on-one, according to Grove?
The manager
The HR department
The report, who sets its agenda
The whole team
The report prepares the meeting and chooses the topics; the manager listens and brings experience.
What is Grove's model for group decisions?
The boss decides alone, then informs
Free discussion, clear decision, full support
Majority vote
Mandatory consensus
People debate freely, the decision is made clearly, then everyone supports it, including those who disagreed.
What does “task-relevant maturity” mean?
The report's age
Their seniority in the company
Their level of experience with a given task, which determines the right management style
Their level of education
The same person can be an expert on one subject and a beginner on another: the style must adapt to each task.
According to Grove, when are cultural values the best mode of control?
When the situation is simple and everyone follows their own interest
When the situation is complex, uncertain and people are group-oriented
When you want to cut costs
When the rules are written down
The market suits simple exchanges; shared values work better in complex, ambiguous situations.
